transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Well, my sister actually made the appointment. I guess what brings me in is that my body just feels completely out of my control lately. Like, at first, I was pacing around my apartment all night, just walking back and forth making all these notes for a supper club I want to start. Because I'm a waiter right now, but I took some business classes in college before I left, and you wouldn't believe how poorly most restaurants design their tasting menus. The profit margins are just terrible, and people don't even appreciate the ingredients. I had this whole concept for a late-night underground dining thing... 

But yeah, I was pacing all night doing that. And now? Lately I'm just so... slowed down. Like, my sister was getting so mad at me today because she says it takes me forever just to get my shoes on. Which is weird because they're just regular boots, you know, the kind with the little side zipper? She actually bought them for me for my birthday last year. But I just sit there staring at them and I can't seem to move fast enough.
Have you recently experienced a period where you felt abnormally happy or irritable?

Happy? I don't know if happy is the right word, but yeah, right after I got fired from the restaurant, I just felt... weirdly unstoppable, you know? Like super excited about everything. Which is crazy because getting fired usually sucks, but my manager, Greg—he's this guy who always wears these really loud Hawaiian shirts even though it's a high-end steakhouse, which never made sense to me. Like, if you're charging sixty bucks for a ribeye, maybe wear a tie? It's just unprofessional. 

But anyway, I felt so energized and just... great after he let me go. I had all these massive plans. But then, if anyone—like my sister—if she even slightly questioned my ideas or told me I needed to slow down, I would just absolutely blow up at her. Just start yelling. It felt like she was actively trying to ruin my life and sabotage my potential, just like Greg did when he fired me over a spilled tray of water glasses. Which wasn't even my fault, the floor was wet near the ice machine because the dishwasher always leaves the mop bucket out...
How long did you feel that unstoppable, excited feeling after getting fired?

I don't really know exactly how long it lasted. A few weeks? Maybe more? Time just felt really... squishy, you know? Like I wasn't really sleeping anyway, so the days just sort of bled into each other. I remember I started repainting my kitchen cabinets right after it happened. I went to the hardware store at, like, 6 AM because I couldn't wait, and the guy working the paint counter—he had this huge, bushy beard, like a lumberjack, but he was wearing these tiny wire-rimmed glasses. It just looked so mismatched, you know? Like he couldn't decide if he was chopping wood or reading poetry. 

Anyway, I bought this color called "Electric Citrus," which in hindsight was way too bright for a tiny galley kitchen. My landlord is probably going to be furious, but he hasn't even fixed the leaky faucet in the bathroom yet, and I've asked him three times. The water just goes *drip... drip... drip* all night, and when you're awake at 4 AM, it sounds like a hammer hitting an anvil. So I figured, if he's not going to fix my sink, I can paint the cabinets whatever color I want. But yeah, I guess I felt that way for a while. I just couldn't stop doing things.
Are you currently feeling sad or empty most of the day?

Sad? I don't know if sad is the right word, but... I mean, I guess I just feel like there's nothing in there right now. Like I'm just hollowed out. Which is exactly how I felt when I had to hollow out all those pumpkins for my sister's Halloween party two years ago. She insisted on having real jack-o'-lanterns, but she hates the smell of the pumpkin guts, so guess who had to do all the scooping? Me. And the seeds get stuck under your fingernails, and no matter how much you wash your hands, they still smell like raw squash for days. I tried using that lemon-scented dish soap—the one with the little duck on the label? I always thought that duck looked a little too smug for a cleaning product. Like, what do you know about grease, you're a cartoon bird. But anyway, yeah, I just feel kind of empty, like somebody scooped all my energy out and threw it in the trash.
How long have you been feeling slowed down like this?

Three months? Yeah, about three months. It just hit me like a wall. That heavy, slowed-down feeling, just... dragging everything out. It’s been three months of just feeling like I'm moving through wet concrete. Which reminds me of when they were fixing the sidewalk outside my apartment building last summer. They had this whole crew out there, and they poured the concrete, but they didn't block it off right. So this lady walking her poodle—one of those really fluffy white ones that look like a cotton ball with legs—she just walked right into it. The dog was fine, but her shoes were completely ruined. They were these red heels, too, which is a weird choice for walking a dog at 10 in the morning, right? Like, where are you going in red heels on a Tuesday? But anyway, she was screaming at the construction guys, and they were just standing there looking at her like she was crazy. I watched the whole thing from my window because I couldn't sleep. But yeah, it’s been about three months of just... feeling like I can't move.
Have you experienced any thoughts or heard any voices that weren't there, or seen things that others couldn't see, during these periods of feeling unstoppable or slowed down?

Voices? No, I haven't heard anything like that. Or seen things, no. I mean, unless you count the ticket printer at the restaurant. I wait tables, and that machine makes this awful, aggressive *ch-ch-ch* sound that literally gets stuck in your head. You'll be at home trying to sleep and you still swear you hear it going off with a new table's order. It's like phantom ring syndrome, you know? Like when you think your cell phone is vibrating in your pocket but it's actually not. 

I had this sociology professor back when I was taking classes who did a whole lecture on phantom phone vibrations. He was a weird guy, he wore these thick corduroy jackets with the leather patches on the elbows. I always thought that was just a joke from movies, but he actually wore them in real life. And he'd always pace back and forth across the front of the room while he talked, dragging his left foot just a tiny bit. It drove me absolutely crazy because my freshman roommate used to drag his feet exactly like that, especially when he'd go into our kitchenette at 2 AM to eat my cereal. He'd eat all the marshmallows out of my Lucky Charms and then just leave the bag wide open so the rest of it got completely stale. I mean, who does that? It's just disrespectful. But anyway, what were we talking about? Oh, right, voices. No, I haven't been hearing or seeing anything that isn't really there. Just the normal stuff.
Have you experienced any thoughts or heard any voices that weren't there when you were feeling slowed down?

No, still no voices or anything when I'm in that slump. I mean, I know you probably have to double-check, but it kind of reminds me of my manager at the restaurant, Gary. He always asks if we rolled the silverware, even if he literally just watched me do it five minutes ago. He's got this weird obsession with the silverware station. And he insists we use these specific cheap paper napkins that tear if you even look at them wrong. I swear, the owner must be getting a discount from some shady napkin supplier. Like, who buys one-ply napkins for a sit-down restaurant? If somebody orders the ribs, they need at least ten of them just to get the barbecue sauce off their fingers. 

The barbecue sauce there is actually pretty good, though. It's got this sweet, smoky hickory flavor. I'm pretty sure they put molasses in it. My grandma used to bake with molasses when I was a kid. She made these gingerbread cookies every winter that were basically hard as rocks. You had to dunk them in milk or coffee just so you wouldn't break a tooth on them. I don't even drink coffee anymore, honestly, it just makes my stomach hurt and makes me jittery. But yeah, to answer your question, no. When I'm feeling all slowed down like that, my head is actually just really quiet. No voices or anything.
When you're feeling slowed down and empty, do you ever think about death or suicide?

Death? Um, no, not really. I mean, it's more like I just don't want to exist, you know? Like I just want to pause everything. But not like, actually killing myself. It's just so exhausting being that heavy. Which is exactly how I felt when I had to help my buddy Mark move out of his third-floor walk-up last month. 

He had this massive, solid oak dresser that must have weighed three hundred pounds. I don't even know how he got it up there in the first place. Probably hired professionals, which is what he should have done this time instead of buying us pizza and cheap beer as a bribe. He always gets that terrible pizza from the place on 4th Street, the one where the cheese slides off in one big greasy sheet as soon as you pick up a slice. It's like eating a hot, salty slip-and-slide. I told him we should have ordered from Antonio's instead, because they actually season their sauce, but Mark is so cheap. He's always been like that, even back in high school when he'd try to negotiate the price of a soda at the vending machine. Like, it's a machine, Mark, it doesn't care about your bargaining skills. 

But anyway, yeah, I don't think about suicide or anything. It's just... I just want to lay there and not have to do anything. Like not even breathe if I didn't have to. But not actually dying.
When you're feeling slowed down and empty, have you experienced any thoughts or heard any voices that weren't there?

Wait, didn't you just ask me that? Like a couple minutes ago? But yeah, still no. No voices or anything like that when I'm feeling all heavy and empty. It's actually completely silent. 

You repeating the question kind of reminds me of my car radio, though. I drive this beat-up 2008 Honda Civic, and the tuning dial is completely jammed. It's stuck on this one classic rock station, and I swear they play "Hotel California" every single day at exactly 4 PM. It's like they only have ten songs on their entire playlist and just run them on a loop. 

I actually went to California a couple of years ago. San Diego. It was supposed to be this great trip, but the ocean was freezing. And I bought this massive, warm churro on the boardwalk, right? I took maybe one bite, and this giant seagull literally dive-bombed me and snatched it right out of my hand. Just grabbed it and flew off. Seagulls are basically just rats with wings, I swear. My friend Mark—the guy who made me move that heavy oak dresser I was just telling you about—he tried to chase the bird down to get it back, but he tripped over some guy's beach umbrella and completely wiped out in the sand. It was hilarious, but I was still pretty mad about the churro. They were like six bucks each. 

But anyway... what were we saying? Oh, the voices thing. Yeah, no, nothing like that. Just totally quiet.
Have you experienced any thoughts or heard any voices that weren't there when you're feeling slowed down and empty?

Are you... are you messing with me right now? You literally just asked me that. Like, twice. Seriously, doc, no voices. Nothing. When I'm in that slump, it's just quiet. 

Honestly, this is starting to feel like that time I tried to cancel my gym membership. Have you ever tried to do that? It's impossible. I called them, and the guy on the phone—his name was Brad, sounded like he drank protein shakes for every meal—he kept asking me the same questions over and over. "Are you sure you want to cancel? What if we freeze your account? What if we give you a free month?" Like, dude, I haven't been to the gym in eight months, a free month isn't gonna magically make me want to go use the elliptical. 

And the ellipticals there are always broken anyway. They make this horrible squeaking noise, like a dying mouse, every time you step on the pedal. It's so distracting. I tried wearing headphones to drown it out, but my earbuds are those cheap ones from the gas station, and the left one only works if you hold the wire at a very specific angle. If you let go, it just cuts out. I bought them when I was driving up to the city for a concert and forgot my good ones. It was that indie band, The Paper Kites? The lead singer was wearing this ridiculous oversized hat the whole time. It looked like a lampshade. 

But yeah, anyway, you don't need to keep asking. No voices, no weird thoughts. Just me and the quiet.
How many months have you been feeling slowed down and empty?

Um, let's see. The heavy, slowed-down part... that's been there for about three months now. Yeah, three months. I know because it started right around Halloween. I work as a waiter at this diner downtown, and we were doing this stupid promotion where anyone who came in wearing a costume got a free side of onion rings. You would not believe what people will do for three dollars' worth of fried onions. 

This one guy came in wearing one of those giant inflatable T-Rex suits. You know the ones with the little battery-powered fan inside? He couldn't even fit into the booth. He tried to squeeze in and his giant plastic tail knocked over an entire tray of ice waters I had just set down for a six-top. Water everywhere. And of course, I had to mop it up, but the wheels on our mop bucket are completely jammed with, like, years of kitchen grease and hair, so it doesn't even roll anymore. You just have to drag it across the linoleum, and it makes this awful scraping sound that sets my teeth on edge. It's almost as bad as the sound of people chewing ice, which my manager does literally all shift. Crunch, crunch, crunch. It drives me insane. 

But yeah, three months. Since around then.
Have you experienced any thoughts or heard any voices that weren't there when you're feeling slowed down and empty?

Are you... is there a hidden camera in here? Because I swear you're messing with me. That's the third time you've asked me about the voices. Or fourth? I've lost count. But no, still no. No voices, no weird thoughts. Just quiet. 

Honestly, it's starting to feel like I'm stuck in that movie Groundhog Day. You know, with Bill Murray? Where he wakes up to the same Sonny and Cher song every single morning? "I Got You Babe." My mom used to play that song on vinyl when I was a kid. She had this massive record collection in the basement, but the basement always smelled like mildew and old laundry detergent. We had this washing machine that would violently shake during the spin cycle—like, it would literally walk across the floor. You'd go down there to get your clothes and the machine would be blocking the door. 

My brother tried to fix it once by shoving a folded-up piece of cardboard under one of the legs, but he used a piece from a pizza box, and it just got soggy and gross. We ordered from this place called Mario's, and they always put way too much sauce on their pizza. Like, it's basically soup on bread. You take a bite and all the cheese just slides right off and burns your chin. I burned my chin so bad once right before a date, it looked like I had some kind of weird rash. The date was a total disaster anyway. We went to see a movie, but the projector broke halfway through, and we just sat there in the dark for twenty minutes while the staff tried to figure it out. 

But yeah, no voices. I promise. Just me.
Did you experience any thoughts or heard any voices that weren't there when you were feeling unstoppable and excited after getting fired?

No, no voices or anything like that. When I was feeling all revved up after getting fired, it was just me, just my own thoughts going a million miles an hour. It wasn't like someone else was talking to me. 

Though, you know, it's funny you ask about voices, because my neighbor—the guy who lives in the apartment below me—he plays his TV so loud I can hear the dialogue through the floorboards. It's always infomercials, too. Like, three in the morning, and I'm hearing about the magic of some non-stick copper pan. "Eggs slide right off!" It's ridiculous. I actually bought one of those pans once, years ago, when I first moved out. Total scam. The very first time I tried to make a grilled cheese, the bread stuck right to the middle and burned to a crisp. 

I had to scrape it off with a butter knife, and it completely ruined the finish. Which was a bummer, because I love grilled cheese. But you have to use mayo on the outside of the bread, not butter. It gets so much crispier that way. My roommate in college taught me that. He was a culinary arts major, but he dropped out to start a dog-walking business. He had this whole fleet of custom leashes he made out of climbing rope. Really sturdy stuff, but they smelled terrible when it rained. 

But yeah, no weird voices or anything when I was feeling unstoppable. Just me.
Have you experienced any thoughts or heard any voices that weren't there when you're feeling slowed down and empty?

Wait, seriously? Are you reading off a broken script or something? Because you literally just asked me that exact same question a minute ago. The slowed down and empty one. I really feel like I'm taking crazy pills today. But no, still no. No voices, no weird thoughts. Just me. 

Speaking of pills, though, my aunt used to keep all her vitamins in this giant plastic organizer that looked exactly like a tackle box. She had one of those actual tackle boxes too, because she loved fishing. She'd take me out on this aluminum rowboat at five in the morning, and the metal seats would be freezing cold. You'd sit down and it would just shock your whole system. We never even caught anything good, just these tiny little sunfish that we'd have to throw back. 

One time she actually hooked a rubber boot. Like an actual, literal cartoon boot covered in green algae. It smelled worse than the dumpster behind the diner on a Tuesday in July, which is really saying something because Tuesday is the fried seafood special day. The smell just gets baked into the asphalt out back. It's disgusting. The stray cats won't even go near it, and they usually eat anything. There's this one cat with half an ear that always begs by the back door, and I try to sneak him turkey scraps when the manager isn't looking. 

But yeah, to answer you again... no voices. Just quiet.
When you're feeling slowed down and empty, do you have difficulty performing daily tasks like taking a shower or getting dressed?

Yeah, it's... it's really hard. When I get like that, slowed down and empty, my body just feels completely out of my control. Like, lately I'm so slowed down my sister says it takes me forever just to get my shoes on. Which is crazy, because right before this, I was pacing around my apartment all night, literally all night, making these incredibly detailed notes for a supper club I was going to start. 

I had the whole menu planned out. Five courses. The main was going to be this braised short rib with a parsnip purée. Parsnips are so underrated, you know? Everyone always goes for mashed potatoes, but parsnips have this sweet, earthy flavor that just cuts through the richness of the meat. I actually tried growing parsnips in a window box once. Total failure. You need really deep soil for root vegetables, and my apartment only gets direct sunlight for like two hours a day in the afternoon. 

The afternoon sun is the worst, anyway. It hits the TV screen right when Jeopardy is on. I love Jeopardy. I used to watch it with my grandpa every single night. He'd always shout the answers before the contestants even had a chance to buzz in. He was a history teacher, so he knew all the obscure facts about, like, the War of 1812. He had this old wooden cane with a silver handle shaped like a duck's head. I always thought it was a goose, but he was very insistent that it was a duck. 

But yeah, getting dressed or showering? It just feels impossible when I'm that slowed down. Like I'm moving through wet cement.
When you're feeling slowed down and empty, do you have a decreased interest in activities you normally enjoy?

Yeah, definitely. It's like... the stuff that usually keeps me steady, you know? Like cooking, taking photos of the food I make, listening to music, playing pickup soccer on the weekends, even the volunteering I do... it all just feels completely flat. Like, I know in my head that I used to care about all of it, but I just can't make myself feel it anymore. 

Which is really weird, especially with the volunteering, because I usually love going to the animal shelter. They have this one pit bull mix right now named Barnaby. He's got these giant floppy ears that look like they belong on a basset hound, and he always trips over his own paws when he gets excited. It's the funniest thing. I actually tried to adopt a dog once, back when I was a freshman in college. But my dorm had this super strict no-pets policy, obviously. 

I tried to sneak a hamster in instead. I kept him in this plastic bin under my bed, and he had one of those squeaky wheels that just went non-stop all night. My roommate was so mad. He threatened to tell the RA if I didn't get rid of it, so I ended up giving it to this girl in my biology class who had a huge crush on the professor. She'd always sit in the front row and ask these incredibly specific questions about cellular mitosis just to get his attention. I think she ended up dropping out to become a yoga instructor in Costa Rica or something. 

But yeah, everything I usually like doing just feels... I don't know, just empty now.
Did you experience any thoughts or heard any voices that weren't there when you were feeling unstoppable and excited after getting fired?

No, nothing like that. No voices or anything when I got fired. I was just really pumped up, you know? Like I didn't even care that Mr. Henderson let me go. He was such a micromanager anyway. He used to make us waitstaff wear these awful polyester vests that were basically static electricity traps. You couldn't walk past the metal dessert cart without getting shocked. I actually complained about it once, but he just told me it was character building. Character building. 

It was like rubbing a balloon on your head in third grade. I did that for a science fair project once to show how static works, but my poster board got ruined because my mom left it in the trunk of her car and it rained. Her trunk always leaked. It was this old Honda Civic that she bought from my uncle, the one who moved to Arizona to open a cactus nursery. Which is a really weird business model if you think about it, because they literally grow everywhere out there for free. Why would anybody buy a cactus when you can just walk outside and dig one up? He sent us a box of prickly pear jelly once for Christmas and it tasted like sweet dirt. I ended up throwing it away when my mom wasn't looking. 

But yeah, no. I wasn't hearing things or having any weird thoughts that weren't real. I was just feeling really unstoppable.
How often do you experience these periods of feeling slowed down and empty?

Well, this heavy, slowed-down part... it's been going on for about three months now. Just three months of feeling like I'm dragging myself through molasses. Which is funny because I actually tried to make molasses cookies last week. I thought baking might snap me out of it, you know? But I completely burned the first batch because I forgot to set a timer. 

Timers are tricky. I used to have this vintage kitchen timer shaped like a tomato, but the bell inside it broke so it just ticked ominously and never rang. I bought it at a flea market with my buddy Josh. Josh is always finding the craziest stuff at flea markets. Once he bought a taxidermy squirrel that was holding a tiny banjo. He put it on his coffee table, and his cat was absolutely terrified of it. Like, wouldn't even walk into the living room for a week. 

Cats are so weird about stuff like that. I had a cat growing up that was afraid of aluminum foil. If you just crinkled a piece of foil, he would bolt under the sofa and stay there for hours. My dad used to put foil on the kitchen counters to keep him off, but then the cat just figured out how to open the cabinets and sleep on the clean towels instead. 

But yeah, anyway, the slowed-down feeling has been stuck with me for like three months now.
Have you experienced any thoughts or heard any voices that weren't there when you're feeling slowed down and empty?

No, no voices or anything like that. I haven't been hearing things or having any weird thoughts. Just... just the emptiness. It's so quiet, honestly. Too quiet sometimes. Like when you're the last person to leave a movie theater and the credits are done rolling and the lights come up and it's just... dead silent. 

I actually used to work at a movie theater back in high school. Ripping tickets, mostly. It was the easiest job in the world, except when they made me clean the popcorn machine. That grease gets literally everywhere. It's like it bonds to your DNA or something. I'd go home smelling like artificial butter for days. My mom made me leave my uniform in the garage because she couldn't stand the smell. 

She's got this super sensitive nose, my mom. She can smell rain coming like three hours before a cloud even shows up. She says it's because she grew up on a farm in Ohio. They grew soybeans, mostly. I went there once when I was a kid and got chased by a rooster. People think roosters are just these funny farm animals that wake you up, but no, they are dinosaurs. Pure evil. It pecked the back of my knee and I had a bruise for a week. 

But no, to answer your question, no voices or anything strange like that. Just feeling really empty and slow.
How often do you have periods where you feel slowed down and empty, compared to periods where you feel unstoppable and excited?

I mean, I don't really know how to compare them or how often it happens. It just feels like I'm either one or the other, you know? Like right now it's just this heavy, awful slog. But before that, when I was feeling so good... I don't know, it's hard to keep track of time when you're moving that fast. 

Time is a weird concept anyway. Have you ever thought about daylight saving time? It makes zero sense. We all just collectively agree to pretend it's an hour later or earlier because some guy a hundred years ago wanted more sunlight to catch bugs or something. I read an article about that once in a dentist's waiting room. The magazines in waiting rooms are always like three years old. I was at Dr. Patel's office getting a cavity filled—he's got these giant hands, which is terrifying when they're inside your mouth with a drill. He always asks me questions while he's working, and I'm like, "Ah ah ah ah," because my mouth is full of cotton and metal. 

Anyway, I don't really have a good answer for how often it switches back and forth. I just know I'm stuck in the slow part right now.

I don't really know exactly how long it lasted. A few weeks? Maybe more? Time just felt really... squishy, you know? Like I wasn't really sleeping anyway, so the days just sort of bled into each other. I remember I started repainting my kitchen cabinets right after it happened. I went to the hardware store at, like, 6 AM because I couldn't wait, and the guy working the paint counter—he had this huge, bushy beard, like a lumberjack, but he was wearing these tiny wire-rimmed glasses. It just looked so mismatched, you know? Like he couldn't decide if he was chopping wood or reading poetry.

My landlord is probably going to be furious, but he hasn't even fixed the leaky faucet in the bathroom yet, and I've asked him three times.
